Subject: Audit trail exportability, slicing windows & format questions (RFP follow-up)

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement packet for Helix Bank's platform risk team, we need a detailed response on your audit logs / event export capabilities. A few specific asks below — please keep answers technical (for our infosec architects):

1) Export granularity and slicing: can you export raw audit events scoped to a single project/account or API key? Can we slice by timestamp ranges (hour/day/week) and by event type (auth, model_call, admin_action)?
2) Retention windows: what default retention windows do you enforce for hosted customers? Do you support custom retention for enterprise contracts and legal holds?
3) Export formats and integrity: supported formats (JSONL/CSV/Parquet)? Do exports include verifiable integrity metadata (hashes, sequence ids) so we can ingest and validate in our SIEM?
4) Incremental vs full extracts: do you support incremental export deltas with continuation tokens? Is there an API and/or S3 push option?
5) Data residency & key control: can we export without leaving eu/us regions, and do you support customer-managed keys (CMKs) for export bundles?
6) SLA & timing: typical lead time for a full 90-day extract of 500M events? Any throughput/parallelism limits we should plan for?

Can you consolidate into a short technical response and include a sample extract (schema + 1k sample records) if possible. We need this in our RFP package by EOD 17 Sep.

Appreciate it — Erin
Security Architect, Helix Bank

Erin / Tomás — thanks for the detailed asks. Below is a concise technical response followed by operational notes. I've attached a 1k-record sample (audit-export-sample.jsonl) and a short playbook.

Technical answers (high-level):
- Export granularity: Exports can be scoped to customer account, project/namespace, and down to API key or user id. Filtering supports event_type, user_id, api_key, source_ip, and tags. Time-range slicing supports arbitrary start/end timestamps; we also provide convenience windows (hour/day/week) for bulk jobs.
- Retention windows: Hosted default retention is 90 days for high-cardinality event logs and 365 days for aggregated billing/event summaries. Enterprise contracts can request custom retention (e.g., 7yrs) via contract amendment; legal holds suspend normal purging for specified scopes.
- Formats & integrity: Supported export formats: JSONL (default), compressed NDJSON (.jsonl.gz), Parquet (columnar), and CSV (for flat events). Each export bundle includes a manifest.json with sequence ids, per-file SHA256 checksums, byte offsets, and an export-level UUID + timestamp for replay validation.
- Incremental extracts: We provide an export API with start_token / continuation_token for delta exports. For large datasets, we support S3 push (server->customer) with presigned multipart URLs and also a pull API. Export jobs emit progress webhooks and a final manifest.
- Data residency & KMS: Exports are executed in the region of the customer account (us / eu / apac). For Private/Dedicated deployments we can keep all processing on-prem. We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS or HSM-backed envelopes for export archive encryption.
- SLA & throughput: For a 90-day extract of 500M events we recommend using the S3 push path with parallel workers; typical completion 12–36 hours depending on requested compression and account throughput caps. We can provide a committed window under Dedicated contracts; otherwise best-effort with throttling limits to protect shared runtime.

Operational notes / constraints:
- Exports are subject to request authentication via admin API tokens and RBAC — only authorized org-admin roles can request full extracts.
- Real-time exports (nearline streaming) are supported but billed separately; bulk jobs are preferred for historical slices.
- For compliance ingestion, we include an optional signed export manifest (PKCS7) for tamper-evidence.

Attachments included: audit-export-sample.jsonl (1k sample), export-playbook.pdf (operational steps), s3-push-config.yaml (example S3 push configuration).

If you want, we can schedule a 30–45m runbook walk-through and transfer test.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — couple follow-ups from our legal/compliance review:

1) EU residency: Helix must ensure event exports containing EU customer personal data remain within EU region unless explicit transfer is authorized. You mentioned region-scoped exports — can you confirm the export processing path remains inside the EU region (i.e., no control-plane egress)?
2) Key control: for encrypted export bundles we need the ability to use our CMK (AWS KMS) and have logs of key usage. Does your export flow surface KMS usage events?

3) Sample: the sample looks good, but we need a second sample with API-key scoped events (filter api_key=prod-abc123) and a short manifest demonstrating SHA256 values for two files.

Timeline: we still need the RFP packet by COB Friday 17 Sep. Can you provide the additional sample and a one-page confirmation on EU processing path by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks,
Tomás
Head of Platform Risk, Helix Bank
